key_idea: The proof uses the quadratic growth of canonical heights on a rank-one elliptic curve to construct an intermediate growth function, which then bounds and uniquely specifies the index of a Pell equation to yield a single-fold exponential function.
reason: The argument masterfully connects arithmetic geometry (elliptic curve heights) with number theory (Pell equation asymptotics) to solve a fundamental problem in computability. The modular structure cleanly separates the intermediate growth, exponential generation, and machine simulation, resulting in a surprising, deeply conceptual, and inevitable proof.
recognized: Single-fold Diophantine representation of recursively enumerable sets
